verdict.summary: A solid, well-proportioned timber house on stone footings with a dark tiled stepped roof, a stone lantern and a stepping-stone path, so it reads as a Japanese-style building, but the curved eaves are flat slabs and the paper-screen walls are too thin to read as the tea house's signature, and the maple is missing.

issues.problem: Hipped-and-gabled roof reads as a stacked lid; eaves are flat slabs with only small corner tips, not curved eaves
issues.fix: Shape the eave edges with stair blocks that step up and out at each corner, and extend the corner tips so the roofline sweeps upward toward the ends.

issues.problem: No maple tree anywhere in the garden; the green bushes read as generic shrubs
issues.fix: Add a small maple beside the house: a dark-log trunk of 2-3 blocks with a red or orange leaf canopy (e.g. azalea or nether wart shaped), placed off the veranda corner.

issues.problem: Paper-screen walls are sparse thin white strips on the front and back; most of the wall is open dark frame, so the sliding-screen identity is lost
issues.fix: Fill each bay between the dark timber posts with white panels (white wool or quartz slabs) set one block deep, leaving only the sliding tracks as dark lines.

issues.problem: Engawa veranda is only a narrow bench-like strip; it does not read as a continuous timber walkway around the house
issues.fix: Run a full-length slab walkway one block out from the floor along the front and one side, with the same timber as the floor and a post at each corner.

issues.problem: Tall dark post on the right side of the front stands out as an unexplained column; the roof-ridge block is floating
issues.fix: Either tie the post into the veranda structure with a beam at the top, or remove it; set the ridge finial onto a supporting block.
